resume: Submitting a social housing application in Mayotte, getting your unique number, gathering the right documents (including those related to a separation) and renewing the application every year.
aQuoiCaSert: Social housing is housing with a regulated rent, allocated subject to income limits. The application, online or at a registration office, gives you a unique number (numéro unique), which starts the clock on how long your application has been waiting. After a separation, you can have only your own income taken into account, provided you supply the right supporting documents.
quiEstConcerne: Households whose income does not exceed the limits set for the overseas departments, including Mayotte.
Parents who are separating and need to find new housing with their children.
Foreign nationals holding a valid residence permit or receipt (récépissé).
aSavoir: Income limits in the DOM (overseas departments), including Mayotte, for an application made in 2026 (2024 income, general case): €27,382 for 1 person, €36,567 for 2, €43,973 for 3 people or a single person with 1 dependent, €53,088 for 4 or a single person with 2 dependents, €62,450 for 5, €70,383 for 6, plus €7,851 per additional person.

Separation: to have only your income taken into account, attach proof such as the document referring the case to the family court judge (juge aux affaires familiales, JAF), the divorce judgment or the birth certificate noting the dissolution of the PACS (civil partnership).
In the overseas departments, you need one application per department: an application in Mayotte only covers Mayotte.
The application must be renewed every year; without renewal, it is cancelled.
